children: Wholesale inflation was much stronger than expectations last month, posting the largest monthly advance since 2022.
The producer price index for total final demand rose 1.3% in September, translating to growth of 6.3% year over year, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Thursday.
The September increase is the largest advance since March 2022, the BLS reported.

That blew past expectations. Economists surveyed by FactSet expected PPI to rise 0.5% month over month after wholesale inflation rose 0.4% in August. Producer prices were up a revised 5.6% year over year in August.

The hotter-than-expected PPI reading comes after the consumer price index surged last month, making a stronger case for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its policy meeting on Oct. 27-28.
